correctness.rationale: The induced-component cycle test follows by removing the candidate vertex from its cycle, or adjoining it to a simple path between two of its neighbours. A pure subset does not grow; a star has no cycles (including K₁,₁). In a cyclic biclique a mixed pair does not grow and a mixed triple spans by adding vertices in the singleton-represented part via four-cycles, then filling the other part. With at least three parts a cross pair grows via triangles to a third part and then to every vertex. The candidate independent faces in each case have identity hulls on all proper subsets, which directly checks the three predicates. For forbidden sets it suffices by heredity to check mixed four-sets in cyclic bicliques and mixed triples with at least three available parts. For convex dependence delete one vertex leaving a spanning proper subset; for Radon dependence partition off such a subset. In a biclique the mixed four-set has distribution 2+2 or 3+1: in the former all deletion hulls are full, in the latter the only proper deletion hull is the majority triple. In the multipartite case the two distributions are 1+1+1 and 2+1: all deletion hulls are full in the former, and the only proper one is the majority pair in the latter. This also supplies the Helly case when a larger set meets exactly two parts with no singleton part among its selected vertices, a case only implicit in the frozen exposition. The face counts and maxima follow from the surviving pure sets and small mixed sets. Each part simplex is a disjoint contractible CW subcomplex, so collapsing them successively preserves homotopy. For r≥3 the quotient is a connected multigraph with E edges and r vertices. For a cyclic biclique the quotient has two vertices, ab edges and T=a·binom(b,2)+b·binom(a,2) two-cells, and is simply connected because the original contains the full two-skeleton of a simplex. Integral H₂ is free of rank 1−ab+T. Spherical representatives by Hurewicz induce a homology equivalence from the stated wedge, hence a homotopy equivalence by simple connectivity and Whitehead. This is an integral argument and does not depend on the frozen finite mod-2 tests.

value.rationale: Comparing the full independent families distinguishes the graph regimes more sharply than comparing the three maxima. The integral homotopy computation gives a two-sphere wedge with exact multiplicity for every cyclic biclique, in contrast to the circle wedge of the dissociation-shaped multipartite case and the contractible star case. In particular, the bipartite result requires an integral homotopical argument (not just a polynomial match or the frozen mod-two check). The value rests on that topology and its simultaneous interpretation for all three predicates, with the overlapping hull, rank and dissociation results credited above.
residual_risks: No homotopy classification for other graph classes or other convexities follows.
